name: Horologium–Reticulum Supercluster
tagline: The southern sky's great supercluster — a 700-Mly-deep mass concentration second only to Shapley.

facts.label: Second
facts.value: Only to Shapley in local mass

history: The Horologium–Reticulum Supercluster is the southern sky's largest mass concentration — an extended complex of rich clusters spread across more than a hundred million light-years. It rivals the Shapley Concentration as the heaviest nearby structure, and its depth demonstrates that even at nearly a billion light-years the cosmos is still organised into coherent walls and knots rather than fading into uniformity.
